## `pnpm agent`

```text
Usage: pnpm agent ask --agent claude|codex|dsh [options] "<prompt>" | -

Runs one headless turn of another coding agent in this repository and prints
its answer: a second opinion, a review, or a delegated question. Which agents
are installed here: pnpm tools list

Options
  --agent <name>       claude | codex | dsh (required)
  --write              Let the agent edit files (default: read-only). Prefer a
                       git worktree; in the main checkout it edits your tree
  --timeout-min <n>    Stop the agent after n minutes (default 10)
  --bin "<cmd>"        Executable, split on spaces (no shell); default: the
                       tool registry entry, else <agent>
  --out <file>         Save the record here instead of the default
  --task <name>        Save under tasks/<name>/tmp/ (default: the active task;
                       with no active task, logs/<YYYYMMDD>/)
  --json               Print a JSON result instead of the answer
  --help, -h           Show this help (also pnpm agent help)

The prompt is the rest of the command line, or stdin when it is "-".
Exit code: the agent's exit code (1 when it was stopped by the timeout).
```

## `pnpm harness`

```text
Usage:
  pnpm harness sync    write the Codex/DSH files generated from utils/harness/hooks.js
  pnpm harness check   fail when a generated file or .claude/settings.json hooks differ from it
  pnpm harness help    show this help (the default)
```

## `pnpm loop`

```text
Usage: pnpm loop [task] --agent claude|codex|dsh [options]

Re-runs a headless agent until the task's verify commands pass. Runs in a git
worktree: from the main checkout it creates (or reuses) ../<repo>-wt/<task> on
branch loop/<task>, copies the task folder there, and installs dependencies.

Options
  --agent <name>              claude | codex | dsh (required)
  --review                    Code tasks: after verify passes, run the quality
                              loop — review round (reviewer + triage, read-only,
                              fresh agents), fix confirmed must-fix/high
                              findings, at most 2 rounds (AGENTS.md §4.5);
                              needs every step done before the first round
  --reviewer <name>           Agent for the reviewer and the triage (default:
                              --agent; a different one gives a second opinion)
  --max <n>                   Agent iterations at most (default 5; with
                              --review, per build or fix phase)
  --stall <n>                 Stop after n iterations in a row with no progress
                              (no file changes, or the same failure) (default 2)
  --timeout-min <n>           Wall-clock cap for the whole run (default 60)
  --iteration-timeout-min <n> Cap for one agent run (default 20)
  --bin "<cmd>"               Executable to run, split on spaces (no shell),
                              e.g. --bin "npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh"; default: the
                              tool registry entry (pnpm tools list), else <agent>
  --max-budget-usd <n>        Spend cap per iteration (claude only)
  --dry-run                   Print the plan and the first prompt; run nothing
  --help, -h                  Show this help

Exit code: 0 when verify passes (with --review: when the quality loop is
complete), 1 otherwise. Logs: tasks/<task>/loop/run-*/ (iter-N.md; review
rounds: run-*-review/rN-reviewer.md, rN-triage.md)
```

## `pnpm memory`

```text
Usage: pnpm memory [command] [options]

Status
  status                        (the default) Notes, core block size, personalization,
                                saving on/off, warnings
  init                          Create memory/, AGENTS.local.md, CLAUDE.local.md (idempotent);
                                applies memory/persona.md when you keep one

Save and change
  add "<text>" --scope user|machine|repo --type preference|fact|howto|episode
      [--repo <name|path>] [--tags a,b] [--trigger "<pattern>"]… [--pin] [--force]
                                Save a note and print its id. Secrets are refused; a
                                near-duplicate is merged into the old note. A repo note
                                defaults to the current repository (the task's --repo, else
                                this folder). --force saves while saving is off
  edit <id> ["<text>"] [--tags a,b] [--trigger "…"]… [--type …] [--scope …] [--repo …]
                                Change a note (--tags and --trigger replace the old lists)
  rm <id> -m "why"              Delete a note (it stays in the journal)
  pin <id> · unpin <id>         Pinned notes are in every session's core block
  check <id>                    Mark a note confirmed today (no longer stale)

Find
  recall "<query>" [--scope …] [--repo …] [--limit N] [--failure]
                                Search like the hooks do (--failure: the query is an error)
  list [--scope …] [--type …] [--repo …] [--pinned] [--stale] [--all]
                                Browse notes (--all includes deleted ones)
  show <id>                     A note with its source and history
  history [--grep "…"] [--limit N]
                                The journal of changes, oldest first (default: the last 20)

Extraction and consolidation
  extract [<session>] [--dry-run]
                                Extract notes from the queued sessions now (the worker
                                normally does this in the background). <session> extracts
                                a session that is still open; --dry-run prints what would
                                be sent to the model and changes nothing
  inbox [--reset]               Changes extraction held back for you to review (they read
                                like instructions); --reset clears the list
  consolidate [--dry-run]       Tidy the notes and rewrite the profile now (normally weekly,
                                in the background)
  undo [--dry-run]              Revert the last extraction, consolidation, import, or persona
                                compaction (notes saved since are kept)

Move or back up (an explicit step; nothing is synced)
  export [--include memory,personalization,tasks,resources] [--tasks a,b] [--out <file>]
      [--allow-secrets]           Write a .tar.gz with a checksummed manifest (default:
                                memory,personalization to memory-export-<yymmdd>.tar.gz).
                                --tasks requires tasks in --include.
                                Files that look like they hold secrets stop the export
  import <file> [--include …] [--dry-run] [--replace]
                                Validate the archive (paths, links, checksums) before
                                anything is written, then merge: new ids, other machines'
                                notes unchecked, duplicates skipped, your settings, tasks,
                                and resources kept. --replace takes over the store and
                                settings; a snapshot is taken first

Settings
  personalize --show            Show the saved settings and whether they apply (the default)
  personalize --presets         List the available presets
  personalize [--preset <name>] [--call-me …] [--about-me …] [--language …]
      [--persona … | --persona-file <file.md>] [--tone <text|preset>] [--traits a,b]
      [--extra …] [--reset]
                                Set how agents talk to you in conversations. An empty
                                value clears a field. --persona-file reads the
                                persona from markdown (comments and heading marks
                                dropped; the same 1,500-character limit). Keep the
                                persona in memory/persona.md instead and pnpm memory init
                                (or workspace:setup) applies your edits; persona changes
                                here and by import rewrite it
  personalize [--persona … | --persona-file <file.md>] --compact [--dry-run]
      [--agent claude|codex|dsh] Shorten the persona to fit, then audit it in a fresh context.
                                --dry-run writes only memory/persona.candidate.md
  personalize [--persona … | --persona-file <file.md>] --audit [--agent claude|codex|dsh]
                                Check the persona without changing it. Both commands default
                                to Claude and use memory/persona.md or the stored persona
                                when no source flag is given. --agent codex requires
                                zero configured MCP servers
  personalize --off | --on      Pause or resume applying saved personalization across sessions.
                                A new session loads the full settings after --on
  set [--extract-model <model>|default] [--budget <characters>|default]
                                Extraction model and core block budget
  off [--session] · on [--session]
                                Pause automatic saving everywhere, or for this session
                                (incognito); recall still works

Options
  --message <text>, -m <text>   Reason for rm
  --json                       Machine-readable output
  --help, -h                   Show this help (also pnpm memory help)
```

## `pnpm skills:install`

```text
Usage: pnpm skills:install [options]

Install third-party skills listed in skills-lock.json.

Options
  --only <names>  Install only these skill names (comma-separated, repeatable)
  --skip <names>  Exclude these skill names (comma-separated, repeatable)
  --help, -h     Show this help
```

## `pnpm skills:link`

```text
Usage: pnpm skills:link [options]

Link the workspace's skills into harness directories.

Options
  --target <dir>  Link into this directory (repeatable, default .claude/skills)
  --check         Verify links and exit 1 if any need repair
  --json          Print a JSON report
  --help, -h      Show this help
```

## `pnpm swarm`

```text
Usage: pnpm swarm [task] --agent claude|codex|dsh [options]

Runs the task's steps with parallel headless workers. Each worker claims a
ready step (dependencies done; same lock as pnpm task claim), works in its own
worktree ../<repo>-wt/swarm-<task>--<step> branched from the integration
branch swarm/<task>, and must leave the task's verify passing. The swarm
commits each finished step on its step branch and merges it into
swarm/<task>; at the end it runs verify there. Review and merge swarm/<task>
yourself. Failed steps are marked blocked (their dependents wait).
Only git-tracked code moves between workers: a task that keeps code in its
(git-ignored) task folder is refused — use pnpm loop for it instead.

Options
  --agent <name>              claude | codex | dsh (required)
  --workers <n>               Parallel workers, 1–8 (default 2)
  --fix <n>                   Fix-until-green iterations per step after the
                              first run, 0–50 (default 3)
  --stall <n>                 Stop a step after n fix iterations with no
                              progress (default 2)
  --timeout-min <n>           Wall-clock cap; no new claims after it (default 120)
  --iteration-timeout-min <n> Cap for one agent run (default 20)
  --bin "<cmd>"               Executable to run, split on spaces (no shell);
                              default: the tool registry entry, else <agent>
  --max-budget-usd <n>        Spend cap per agent run (claude only)
  --no-install                Skip pnpm install in new worktrees
  --dry-run                   Print what would run; start nothing
  --help, -h                  Show this help

Exit code: 0 when every step is done and the final verify passes, else 1.
Logs: tasks/<task>/swarm/run-*/ (<step>.log, <step>.result.json)
```

## `pnpm task`

```text
Usage: pnpm task <command> [options]

Start / resume
  status [name]                 Resume brief: goal, next step, last notes, verify, git
  list [--all]                  Tasks with status and next step (--all includes done)
  switch <name>                 Make <name> the active task
  new <name> --goal "…"         Create tasks/<name>-<yymmdd>/ and make it active
      [--acceptance "…"] [--step "…"]… [--verify "cmd"]… [--verify-fast "cmd"]…
      [--kind code|general] [--e2e required|no] [--repo <path>]
                                --kind code (the default when --verify is given): the
                                inner loop starts on and pnpm task check runs before verify;
                                --repo: the git repository the task works in, when it is
                                not this workspace (git state, notes, review scope)
  init [name] [--goal "…"] [--verify "cmd"]… [--verify-fast "cmd"]…
      [--kind code|general] [--e2e required|no] [--repo <path>]
                                Add state.json to a hand-written task (steps from plan.md)

Work
  next [name]                   Print the next ready step
  claim [id]                    Atomically take the next ready step (or <id>) for --agent;
                                exit 2 when nothing is ready (prints why)
  step add "title" [--deps s1,s2]
  step <id> start|done|blocked|waiting [--gate]|todo [-m "…"] [--force]
                                Update a step (blocked needs -m "reason"; waiting = on
                                someone else, needs -m "who does what"; --gate: the wait
                                holds the review, e.g. design approval before any code;
                                todo releases a claim; --force takes over a step another
                                agent claimed)
  step <id> remove -m "why"     Remove a step written by mistake
  note [--done "…"] [--next "…"] [--open "…"] [-m "…"] [--learn "…"]…
                                Append a NOTES.md entry with an automatic State line.
                                Supply at least one of --done, --next, --open, or -m.
                                Each --learn line is saved to memory as a fact with the
                                task as its source (a repo fact for a --repo task)
  check [name] [--fix]          Lint (ESLint), format-check (Prettier), and typecheck (tsc)
                                the task's code; --fix rewrites what ESLint/Prettier can fix
  verify [--fast] [--no-check]  Run the task's verify commands; exit 1 on failure. Tasks
                                with code run pnpm task check first (--no-check skips it)
  set [--goal "…"] [--verify "cmd"]… [--verify-fast "cmd"]…
      [--kind code|general] [--e2e required|no] [--repo <path>|none]
      [--loop on|off] [--loop-max N]
                                Change one or more task settings. Each verify list replaces
                                its previous list. Setting kind to code turns the loop on.
                                Changing --repo records a new start commit for reviews.
                                The inner loop retries until the fast verify passes or the
                                iteration cap is reached (default 5).
  review [--base <ref> | --folder] [--force]
                                Code tasks: open the next review round (max 2) and write the
                                brief + findings file for clean-context reviewers. Scope: the
                                task's code (no git), else git changes since --base (default:
                                the default branch as fetched, e.g. origin/main, else main;
                                for work committed on it, the commit the task started from;
                                an explicit --base is used as given). --folder: the task
                                folder's code, this round and the next
  review record [file]          Read the triaged findings table; CONFIRMED must-fix/high
                                findings become fix: steps
  rm <path>…                    Delete files or folders inside this workspace or the task's
                                repo without asking: they move to tasks/.trash/<time>/ for
                                7 days (refuses .git, task records, secrets, and
                                folders that hold a .git or secrets)
  template review|study [--name <kebab>]
                                Copy a REVIEW_/STUDIES_ template into the task
  done [name] [-m "…"] [--learn "…"]… [--force]
                                Close the task (needs every step done and a passing verify;
                                code tasks also a finished review loop; --force overrides).
                                Saves a task digest to memory (goal, outcome -m, open items,
                                --learn lines); closing a reopened task replaces it
  reopen [name] -m "why"        Reopen a closed task: active again and bound to this session;
                                verify and the inner loop start over, and its reviews cover
                                the work from now on (2 more rounds)

Options
  --task <name>                Act on <name> instead of the active task
  --agent <name>               Who is acting (default: $TASK_AGENT, "claude" in Claude Code, else "agent")
  --message <text>, -m <text>  Note or reason for a state change
  --json                       Machine-readable output
  --help, -h                   Show this help (also pnpm task help)
```

## `pnpm tools`

```text
Usage: pnpm tools <command> [options]

What this machine can call: other agents (claude, codex, dsh), CLIs, runtimes,
and source checkouts of reusable tools. tools/catalog.json (committed) lists
tools worth having; tools/local.json (git-ignored) records what is here.

Commands
  list [--all] [--kind agent|cli|runtime|source]
                         Recorded tools; --all adds install hints for missing ones
  scan [--reset]         Find catalog tools on PATH and record them (manual entries kept;
                         --reset starts from an empty registry)
  check                  Re-run every recorded tool's check; exit 1 if any is broken
  show <name>            Details: path, version, headless usage, install hint
  add <name> [--kind agent|cli|runtime|source] [--path <p>] [--command "<cmd>"]
      [--via "how installed"] [--check "argv"] [--headless "…"] [--env A,B]
      [--message "notes" | -m "notes"] [--task <name>]
                         Record a tool using --path, --command, or both.
                         A source checkout requires --path <directory>.
                         If the tool is in the catalog, --kind defaults to its catalog kind.
  remove <name>          Forget a tool (does not uninstall anything)
  sources                Print the directory for source checkouts

Options
  --json      Machine-readable output
  --help, -h  Show this help (also pnpm tools help)

Call another agent: pnpm agent ask --agent <name> "…". Never put secrets in the
registry; --env records env var names only.
```

## `pnpm workspace:setup` and `pnpm workspace:check`

```text
Usage: pnpm workspace:setup [options]
       pnpm workspace:check [options]

Options:
  --check           Verify only; change nothing (exit 1 if a required step fails)
  --skip-install    Do not run pnpm install
  --skip-skills     Do not install third-party skills from skills-lock.json
  --with-browsers   Install agent-browser's browser and Playwright Chromium (setup only)
  --target <dir>    Extra skill link directory (repeatable), e.g. .dsh/skills
  --json            Print a JSON report
  --help, -h         Show this help
```
